methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Critical Energy, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Spencer Jackson, has raised $22M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector—one public (LNZA) and eight private companies including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable valuation lever. Using the $22M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression in frontier energy ventures, this method implies a valuation of $55M. A Peer-Median approach could not be meaningfully applied; while eight same-sector peers exist, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables. Three or more tight peer datapoints are required to reduce median-based estimation error.

The triangulated valuation range is $47M (low) to $63M (high), with $55M as the median point. This range reflects the single methodological input and therefore carries material uncertainty. Key dependencies include whether the 2.5x Seed step-up multiplier remains appropriate given Critical Energy's specific capital efficiency, competitive positioning, and path to Series A, and whether tighter peer comps will emerge as additional Climate & Energy frontier-tech companies reach similar funding or disclosure milestones.
